newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call money shade up, C Bank maintains rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila call money shade up, C Bank maintains rate.

text.p: * Done rates range from 11.75 to 11.53125 percent.
Manila overnight money was slightly up at an average of 11.5625 percent on Tuesday from 11.53125 percent due to the covering of positions by small banks, traders said.
After the scare caused by the ailing Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank, other small banks may have run into some temporary problems, one trader said.
The market was liquid with 30 lenders and 20 borrowers. Volume was at 18.27 billion pesos from 25.66 billion pesos.

The Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 11.50 percent, traders said. The Central Bank imposed a 0.50 percentage-point increase in its key rate on Monday in order to tame peso speculation due to fears of capital flight from stock market sales.
Dealers predicted the Central Bank would maintain this rate for a week until the stock market showed a convincing trend towards recovery.
In the secondary market, banks were trying to get hold of six-month and one-year bills to lock in higher profits for the longer-term.
Banks, however, were unloading their two-year notes because of the expected increase in its rate at the auction later today.
The two-year coupon rate could fetch a rate of 12 to 13 percent from last month's 11.50, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of seven financial institutions gave bid rates of 11.65 to 12.10 percent for the one-year bills.
